utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-99-36-R77, The Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin concerning allegations against Milka Maglov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Brenda J. Hollis appearing as amicus curiae prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And of course, Ms. Jevtovic -- sorry, Ms. Maglov, I want to make sure first that you can follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand. In other words, that you are receiving proper interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you are being -- you are representing yourself, but also assisted by Ms. Marela Jevtovic. Correct. So before we proceed with the witness, there are two things that I need to raise. One is, Registrar, please, I would like to know if the Registrar has responded or what the Registrar has done with respect to Ms. Maglov's application for legal aid, because we are proceeding in a case and I have heard nothing so far. And since I see nobody in the courtroom assisting Ms. Maglov, I take it that a decision has not yet been taken, and I want to know where we stand.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will get back to you after the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's number one. Second thing, is this, Ms. Maglov: The Prosecution has, I take it, will conclude today, and then the ball is in your court. You need to decide first and foremost whether you are going to tender your own evidence. There is no hard and fast rule of this Tribunal as to when you need to tender your evidence if you choose to do so, but the practice has been and there are some dicta from -- by this Tribunal, also some dicta by this Tribunal that although the legal possibility of testifying at the end, or that is, after the witnesses -- your witnesses have testified exists, that may carry some weight in the minds of the Judges that have to, then, make deliberations and reach conclusions. Most jurisdictions, as you know, if the accused chooses to give evidence, that needs to be done before any of the witnesses for the Defence take the witness box. In other words, first the accused gives evidence, and then the accused's witnesses will follow. But there is no rule specifying that in this Tribunal, although it is most of the time advantageous if you do that. So I don't want a reply from you now. I will let the Prosecution finish its case first, and then you will tell me. But I'm raising this issue now because if you decide to give evidence and if Ms. Jevtovic also is going to give evidence, she is indicated as one of the witnesses, perhaps we could hear that testimony tomorrow so that on Monday when the other witness or witnesses turn up, we will not be burdened with the problem of trying to finish them in one day or having problems if that is not possible. Okay? So think about this, please, and come back to me later on. In the meantime, I think we can bring in the witness. Usher. Yes, we go into closed session. We draw down the curtains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we go into open session, please. And could you admit the next witness, Mr. Ukropina, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you sure he's in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Unless he decided to go home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to make sure that the witness is in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was in the waiting during the last break, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was in the waiting room at the last break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, may I know how long you anticipate this witness to last on direct?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: 10 or 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm asking this because of the break. Interpreters and technicians, shall we finish this witness and then have the break immediately after?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters say yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Technicians? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Welcome back. You are about to give evidence. You know what the procedure is. You have the text of the solemn declaration that is -- you are expected to make under our Rules. Please proceed, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you, sir. Please, take a chair. In the meantime, I notice Mr. Van de Vliet from the Registrar's Office. I had asked him to be kind enough to come up so that he give us the information I requested earlier on, on the possible decision of the Registrar regarding the respondent's request for assignment of counsel. Unfortunately, I thought that he would make the statement much earlier on. I didn't anticipate the testimony of the previous witness to take the length of time it took. So I apologise to you if I kept you waiting there. Perhaps we can dispose of this straight away and then proceed with the interrogation of the witness. Yes, I just wanted to know, Mr. Van de Vliet, whether the Registrar has taken a decision on Ms. Maglov's application to be assigned counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DE VLIET
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have not taken a decision yet. We're still calculating the exact numbers, which to be included and which not. I can give you a preliminary assessment if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we are interested in a preliminary assessment. We want a definitive answer. And may I enjoin you, please, to chase this matter up. The Prosecution case is coming to an end today, and potentially as from tomorrow Ms. Maglov can start with her Defence case. So if a decision is taken in time to at least present her with what the situation is on this matter, I think it's -- it would be very helpful. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DE VLIET
utterances.text: We could have the decision ready by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. In which case, please have it communicated to Ms. Maglov and to our officers and also Ms. Hollis and the Registrar. Thank you. Again, sorry for having kept you waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DE VLIET
utterances.text: That's okay. [Technical difficulty].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Ms. Hollis, the witness is all yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: My name is Dejan Ukropina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I am an attorney-at-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, were you assigned to act as amicus curiae investigator in this matter?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the decision of the Court on the 23rd of April, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And as part of your duties as amicus curiae investigator, did you interview the respondent in this case, Ms. Milka Maglov?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, because I was... We are missing all the questions that have been put to the witness and all his answers in the transcript. I suggest you start again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Shall I start again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you have to start from the very beginning. Ask the witness his name. Start as if he has just walked into the room, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your name.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: My name is Dejan Ukropina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I'm an attorney-at-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And were you assigned to act as amicus curiae investigator in this matter?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, I was, by a court decision dated the 26th of April 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And as part of those duties, did you interview the respondent in this case, Ms. Milka Maglov?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was part of my job, and I did indeed conduct an interview with Ms. Maglov.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when did you conduct that interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, it was on the 23rd of May 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what procedure did you follow in conducting that interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: A few days before that, I spoke to Ms. Maglov on the telephone, and I announced my visit so that we would agree on an exact time and place for recording the interview and for conducting the interview actually. Just before the interview, of course, I introduced myself, and I explained on the basis of what authority I was acting, and I explained the role I was playing and the procedure involved. And I drew the attention of Ms. Maglov to Rules 43 and 44 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence; that is to say, having an audiorecording made, and also the possibility that her statement, either in written form or in audio form could be used later before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you advise Ms. Maglov of her rights as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how did you advise her of her rights as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: The Registry of the ICTY, when I was taking over the documentation related to the case, I got the text of the document itself, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. So everything that I advised Ms. Maglov on was what I read out of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could ask that the witness be shown Rule 42 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence rights of suspects during investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, usher, please. In what language are you showing it to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: In English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you read English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do read English. I do speak English. Seven months ago, I was appointed permanent court interpreter for the English language at the district court in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So look at Rule 42, please. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, is this the Rule that you read to Ms. Maglov when you conducted the interview of her?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what language did you conduct the interview with Ms. Maglov?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I spoke to Ms. Maglov in the Serbian or Bosniak language. That is to say, the language that we both speak and understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you audiotape this interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes. The interview was recorded on audio cassettes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when did you begin the recording of this interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I began the recording of this interview as soon as I advised Ms. Maglov of her rights in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And why did you not begin at the very -- at the very beginning of your interview with her, when you advised her of her rights? Why did you not include that on the tape?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: The beginning of May 2002, when I came to the Tribunal in order to pick up the documents pertaining to this case, and when I spoke to the representatives of the Registry about the procedure itself, one of my questions was whether that part of the interview should be recorded on this audio cassette. However, I was instructed that it was sufficient that I should inform my interlocutor of her rights, that that part did not have to be recorded, but that the entire interview, that is to say from the very beginning of the interview up to the very end of the interview, had to be recorded. So that is the reason why I did not record this on the audio cassette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope whoever gave you this advice is not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And sir, what did you do with the audiotape after you had completed your investigation?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: After I completed my investigation, I handed over the tape to the representatives of the Registry of the Tribunal. That was when I submitted my report as well; namely, on the 19th of June 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown Exhibit P11 and 11.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, have you had the opportunity to review these documents prior to coming into the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And are these two documents the record of interview of your interview with Ms. Maglov in English and in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, those are the records of our interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in the transcript, there are comments or questions by an unidentified male voice. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you will look at the exhibit in English, it is the -- page 1, the 12th and 13th lines of the text; in B/C/S, on page 1 it is the 12th line of the text. There appears the name Milos Ostojevic. Is the surname there correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: The last name is not correct. Ms. Maglov referred to our colleague, Milos Peric, during the interview. So this Ostojevic was not a last name that did crop up during the interview. It is Milos Peric. I assume that this error is perhaps due to the poor quality of the audiorecording.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, based on the interview you conducted with Ms. Maglov, did you prepare a statement for her review and signature?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes. After the interview was Ms. Maglov, on the basis of the audiorecording and the interview, I wrote this out in the B/C/S language. And afterwards, I translated it into the English language. So there were two written statements, one in B/C/S and the other one in English, the texts being identical.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown Exhibit P10 and 10.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Whose signatures, sir, appear on this statement in English and in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: There are two signatures on every page of each statement. One is the signature of Mrs. Milka Maglov, and the other one is my signature, and also my official stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you will look at the last page of each statement, the page that begins with "witness acknowledgment" --

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: That's the signature of Ms. Maglov.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, what procedure did you follow before the respondent signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: A procedure similar to the one when the interview was agreed upon. First, I called, and I said when the interview would take place. And then I explained to Ms. Maglov that this is when the statement would be signed. Actually, during the interview, I said to Ms. Maglov that in about ten days or in a week, I will be coming for the signatures. When we met, I gave Ms. Maglov the B/C/S version, and I said to her that she would absolutely have all the time she needed to read out the statement and to possibly give some comments or remarks if she considers them necessary, and that if there are any remarks, objections, or suggestions, we would correct them right there on the spot, in both versions, in both languages. That is why I took the statements in electronic form, on floppy disks, so that we could correct them. Also, I took the cassette player, the Dictaphone and the cassettes themselves so we could listen to the interview again and perhaps clarify certain points. Ms. Maglov read the statement in B/C/S, perhaps for about 15 minutes or perhaps a bit longer than that. Afterwards, she said that that was the statement that she had given earlier on and that I had recorded on an audio cassette. After, that I asked her to sign the statement, and she did so by signing every page of the statement, three copies in B/C/S and three copies in English. After that, I affixed my own signature with the official stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: So she read the statement herself. It was not read to her.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Precisely. She read the statement herself. Nobody interrupted her while she was reading the statement. No one else was present except for the two of us in the room, and we were not disturbed by anyone walking into the room or a telephone call or in any other way. So I gave her all the time she wanted and all the time she considered necessary so that she could read the statement in peace.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did she take exception to any language in the statement?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: No, she had absolutely no objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did she ask to clarify any matters or to add any additional comments?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: There was no request on her part whatsoever so that the statement was signed in the version that I initially brought. There was no request whatsoever to make any amendment or change in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, have you had occasion to compare the English and B/C/S versions of the interview, the record of interview, with the English and B/C/S versions of the statement signed by respondent?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: When drafting the written statement, which was made by me based on the audiorecording, first in the B/C/S, I translated that text into English. So we are talking about two completely identical texts in two different languages. When recording the interview, I explained to Ms. Maglov that the B/C/S is perfectly identical to the English version, so there was no request for any translation or anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, do you have before you Exhibit P10.1 and 10 and Exhibit P11 and 11.1. Have you had the opportunity to compare those documents?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And it appears when you compare those documents that the language is not exactly the same in the two documents. Can you explain to the Court why the language in the statement is different than some of the language in the record of interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes. When the interview was being recorded, because we are talking about a live recording, Ms. Maglov would sometimes use colloquial expressions or words that are used when you want to give yourself time to think, or she would sometimes digress and move to another subject before returning to the subject we were discussing initially. So I tried to make an accurate reflection of the audiorecording and I was faced with certain sentences that trailed off. And I realised then that a literal copy of the audiorecording word by word would produce a statement that would be sometimes confusing and imprecise. And that is why I tried to make a logical version of her statement using her own sentences that were recorded, not word by word, but without departing from the essence and the gist of what she said and to record truthfully on paper what she said to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said earlier that at the very beginning of your interview, you explained to her your purpose. Did that explanation include that you would be providing this product to the Tribunal, your report of investigation?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes. It was clear to Mrs. Maglov from the very beginning, that the purpose of my contact with her was to conduct an investigation with her as an amicus of the Tribunal and the purpose of producing these documents is to submit them to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hollis, I think we have gone beyond what I thought would be the time that this witness would be testifying. So we need to have a break now to give a rest to the staff and also to have the tapes changed. We'll have a break of 25 minutes starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's start. The legal officer is not here because I sent him to fetch another legal officer with whom I need to speak. Let's continue, yes, Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: As part of your duties as the amicus curiae investigator in this matter, did you conduct interviews with other persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry for that. But we were risking losing the appointment we had on Monday, and I made sure that Monday was still available. Yes, thank you. Yes, Ms. Hollis, my apologies to you, and my apologies to you, sir. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You described the procedure that you followed in regard to conducting the interview with the respondent. Did you follow the same procedure in all the other interviews that you conducted? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, the procedure was absolutely the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you follow the same procedure in preparing statements for these persons' review and signature?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you follow the same procedure when you gave each of these persons their statement to review and sign?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, the procedure was absolutely the same; that is, I left them enough time to read the statement in their mother tongue. And after that, if they would have any comments or suggestions, I let them know that they should feel free to say so. That it was, of course, possible to amend the statements, and modify them, and since none of the persons had any objections or amendments to the statements which were made on the basis of the audiorecordings, they signed their statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And without naming any persons, did you with any of these other individuals you interviewed, did you advise any of them of their rights prior to the commencement of the interview?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I advised each and every one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you follow the same procedure in that advisement that you followed for the respondent?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: The interviews that you conducted with these persons, did you conduct the interview with each person separately?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to each of them separately. And nobody else apart from the interviewee and myself attended these interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Hollis. Ms. Maglov, is there cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I didn't expect that he would be testifying today. But I do have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. But it was -- Ms. Hollis did state yesterday that she would be producing him today. But anyway, go ahead with your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. We met before in Banja Luka. And before we met up in Banja Luka, we met here in the Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. We met before in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Do you remember when we first met in the Tribunal, you gave me a copy of your CV?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I don't recollect that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Do you remember asking me if there was a possibility of us engaging you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: That's possible. It's possible that we talked. It was in January 2002. It was part of a visit by a group of students, together with lawyers and other experts from Serbia who were in the process of establishing the human rights foundation in Serbia, together with some colleagues from Sweden. And a meeting was organised on that occasion with representatives of the Registry and certain Defence lawyers who were already working in the ICTY. And I had several contacts at that time, including the one with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Did you also distribute your CV at the same time to any other lawyers? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't think I did. Actually, sorry, I brought a curriculum vitae that I submitted to the Registry because before that in email contacts with representatives of the Registry, I was informed that I would be included in the list of Defence lawyers and that I was required to bring a letter of reference from the bar association and a CV. So I submitted these documents as soon as I met with the representatives of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Do you remember how many copies you brought?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I think only that one, which I gave to the Registry. I don't remember bringing any other copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Well, you gave me one. Do you allow for the possibility that you had more than one?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I do allow that possibility. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Very well. My next question: During our first interview, I'm talking about the one of the 23rd of May, you came to Banja Luka after calling me by phone, and we met in my office. Who else was in the office? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Mr. Peric and yourself, if my memory serves me well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Before we proceeded to the interview itself, for how long did we talk, you, Mr. Peric, and I?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Well, after the introductions, because it was the first time I saw Mr. Peric, perhaps we had an exchange for about a few minutes. I think it was mostly you and Mr. Peric who did the talking, and you said that the entire procedure that was going on, that was being followed, was a bit odd because you felt that you had done nothing to violate the Rules of Evidence and Procedure. The conversation did not last long because if we had continued to discuss the subject we would have encroached upon the very essence, the very subject of the interview I was supposed to conduct with you and Mr. Peric. Therefore, I said I did not wish to discuss it any longer, that I wanted to carry out the interview, and I asked Mr. Peric to leave the office. And I also said that I would invite him back as soon as the interview was over. After that, I advised you of your rights, and I turned on the voice recorder which is when the interview began.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: If I tell you that on that occasion in the -- in addition to the remarks that you mentioned, we also complained that we did not understand the procedure at all, what did I stress in particular before we proceeded with the interview?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are on cross-examination. You can put a direct question, Ms. Maglov.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Did I make it clear to you in some way on that occasion how it came about that I was suspended? Did I let you know what had happened to me?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I don't remember that you mentioned a specific event, but it is possible that you mentioned that you were suspended. And I think that after the formal interview was over, we continued talking informally whereupon you said that you didn't understand why you were suspended actually, whether it was because of something related to this trial or perhaps the reason was your representation of the said gentleman before a court in Banja Luka. You expressed this doubt at the very end of the interview when I asked you whether you had -- whether you needed any clarification with regard to anything. And that's when you said that you didn't know for sure whether it was in relation to this trial or to your representation of that gentleman in the court in Banja Luka. That's when you made these remarks. And if you allow me a few more words, before the beginning of the interview I advised you of my task and that my duties were limited to investigating the events before September 2001 and that I was not supposed to go into any details of anything that happened before or after or that had to do with any other person.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: If I tell you that after I gave a statement in this case, I actually asked you a question saying that it was not clear to me why I had been suspended, and it was then that I described the other case, because it was mentioned in the decision.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I don't remember what the decision to suspend you said. I remember what was in the document on my appointment as amicus curiae investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: I suppose that we had in our hands the same decisions because what I had was a decision where under item 1 it was said that I was suspended for conflict of interest because I was representing at the same time a witness who had earlier been my client in another case.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I remember that you mentioned something to that effect. And as I said earlier, at the end of the interview, when I asked you if you had any questions, that is when you mentioned as being unclear to you. But I told you on that occasion that I cannot go beyond the limits of my authorisations as specified by the Registry with regard to the investigation in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: All right. Before we proceeded with the interview, my colleague, Mr. Peric, and I discussed this particular case with you.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Well, I allow the possibility that you mentioned it before we began the interview. But the only explicitly expressed doubt was in response to my question whether you wanted to add anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: The statement that you recorded on your Dictaphone is, as you said, a bit confused or confusing, and you revised it, as you put it when translating it into English.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I didn't say that I revised it because the process of revision implies amending the statement. I said that when I recorded your statement on paper, I recorded some sentences which, together, made sense but were not necessarily finished or completely coherent. I recorded them in a coherent way without adding or leaving out any facts or changing in any way the essence of what you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Was my anxiety and the fact that I was visibly upset due to the events that transpired a month earlier?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I allow for the possibility that you were upset. You probably were because you were talking to me, and I was representing the Registry and this Tribunal. And it is possible that you were not completely coherent or articulate at times, which is completely understandable and acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: Is it possible that you came to investigate me on a subject which is completely different from the issue that I understood to be the reason for my suspension?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I don't think that you were confused for that reason because my visit had been announced a few days before that when I telephoned you in this connection. Among other things, I think that the Defence team did receive a decision on my appointment as amicus curiae, so I assume that you received it and that my mandate and my authority and my task were clearly spelled out; that is, what were the facts that I was supposed to throw more light on. So before I came to Banja Luka and before we met, you knew from your conversation with me that we were not discussing conflict of interest in view of the fact that you represented another person earlier on, but that we were talking about the events that took place in September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: What makes it so clear to you that I could have known that? On the basis of what do you know that? If it wasn't clear to me, on what basis was it clear to you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Well, quite simply you said that you knew what we were supposed to talk about. That moment, you were confused because you did not know whether you had been suspended because of one reason or because of both reasons, but you did know that there was a problem of conflict of interest and you were aware that there was a problem due to which we are here today. On that occasion when we met up, I perhaps elaborated to you in greater detail that we would be discussing only part of what you knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: So I was prepared to talk about something else; or rather, at that moment I was not focussed. Was that your impression?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: No, that was not my impression. If we were to simplify matters, you expected us to discuss topics A and B. And when I came, I said that we would only discuss topic B. So I do not believe that you were surprised when I said to you what we would be talking about. You were not confused, and you were not unprepared since Mr. Peric on that occasion, when I called you, asked if he could be present as well, or rather I asked for him to be present so that I could interview him, too. So it was quite clear to you and Mr. Peric that this had to do with the event due to which we are here today.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: All right. Was it all clear to you when I made my statement, when I say "I said," "we said," was it all clear to you who I said this to? I'm just stating this by way of an example. Before we moved on to the interview, I was trying to explain to you indeed that I did not know why all of this happened. Was I perhaps referring to that when I said this?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: It is hard for me to define any answer to your question now. Could you give an example, perhaps, and then I would be in a position to answer, but I believe this is too general. You repeated some facts during the interview that you had referred to during those few minutes before the formal beginning of the interview. And that is precisely why I interrupted you, because I did not want you to talk in an informal conversation about what was supposed to be discussed in the interview, what I was officially supposed to discuss with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: For example, when Peric and I talked to you, we said "we." After our first visit, when we returned to the office, perhaps a month later we saw the statement because we received it only then. And before we went to pay the second visit, we had known that the witness had given a statement to the Prosecution. When I said "we knew" or "I knew," did it pertain to the conversation that the three of us had, my colleague Peric and I, or was it your understanding that I could have said this to X, Y, or somebody else? That is what I have in mind. Because these statements are absolutely ambiguous on that score.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: I think contrary to what you're saying now, your statements were quite clear and precise in that section, when you were talking about whether the Defence team knew about the statement before your visit or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: Mr. Peric said quite explicitly that you did receive the witness statement before you went on your first visit, that at the moment when you went to see him you knew that he was a witness, that he was a Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: If I tell you now that you are absolutely wrong and that is not written in Peric's statement -- If you think that that is what is written there, show me that part of Peric's statement? Let me see it. He claims the contrary, that the first time when we were there we did not know that he was a Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN UKROPINA
utterances.text: That's not the way I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: The statement is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask the Prosecution to show this witness to the statement now. They have the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Usually that would not be regular, but I am pretty sure that Ms. Hollis will cooperate. You normally do not ask the Prosecution to show the witness any of the documents that they have not brought in evidence as yet. Do I take it that you are cooperating in this, Ms. Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. Is Mr. Ackerman out here in the witness room? I think we owe him an explanation, and perhaps also an apology for having kept him there. So if you can send someone to ask him to come over so that I explain to you what's going on, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: I'm providing both the English and the B/C/S version of the interview of 23 May 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. While he goes through the B/C/S version of the statement, can we have the version -- the English version put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, I would like to read part of the statement. On page 2 of Mr. Peric's statement, towards the very bottom of the page. [In English] I can find it. Okay, here. [Interpretation] Mr. Peric says explicitly: "We received his statement, and we were counting on him testifying. We did not consider him to be an important witness that we were supposed to deal with." So Mr. Peric, on that occasion, speaks about the visit paid to Witness R77-B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman, I recognise your presence here in the courtroom. I wanted to explain to you also, apologise to you, for having kept you waiting this long. We had expected the testimony of the previous witnesses to take less time than it actually did. And we should be able to finish with this witness, and that would leave just you. But we won't be able to hear your testimony today, if at all, because I am leaving, of course, on prejudiced matters that might need to be discussed relating to your testimony. But I did want to explain to you why you have been waiting, and I wish to apologise to you for having kept you waiting unduly after that I had asked my staff to enjoin you to be present here as -- at a certain time. Please accept my apologies, and those of the Trial Chamber. Will it be convenient for you to come tomorrow, tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll be here a little before 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I was going to suggest tomorrow we will only have basically you and I don't know if there's going to be anything on the part of the Defence. So I was going to suggest that we start either at 9.30 or at 10.00, which would make it a more decent time for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 9.30 would be fine with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So 9.30. And I think we'll practically start with you. Ms. Maglov, are you about to finish with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I'm sorry, Your Honour, no. I'm not nearing the end. We have another important part left. However, since it's the end of our working hours today, perhaps we can continue tomorrow because not too much time will be required to complete this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So may I suggest, then, that we start at 9.00 tomorrow, just the same. And that we will hear your testimony immediately after this witness finishes, Mr. Ackerman. That should be, I reckon, round about 9.15, 9.30 at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and my apologies once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I didn't wait very long, so it was not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Yes, Ms. Maglov, shall we call it a day, stop here with the cross-examination, and continue tomorrow because I think we have had the rest of the staff here work very hard this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think it would be best to adjourn at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. And once more, I should like to thank the members of the staff, and certainly not least of all the interpreters and the technicians for having patience with us. We'll all meet again, please God, tomorrow morning at 9.00. And I take it Mr. Ackerman will be your last witness. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. May I have an indication, Ms. Maglov, whether you are testifying tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I put some questions in accordance with the Rules, I accept that, yes, I will testify. But before that, I will have some questions, so could that please be borne in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAGLOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's it. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of February, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
